_comment: Per-connection RAM pins (#1228), consumed by bench/ram_census.py. MEASURED values, never round ceilings — a pin left above the truth makes the next growth free. Re-pin ONLY by a deliberate PR edit: python3 bench/ram_census.py gate --conn-raw <transcript> --pins bench/ram_census_pins.json --emit-pins
_instrument: bench_conn_ram --no-can (the CAN arms need a privileged vcan0 the bench host does not carry; can-vcan-e2e.yml owns that path). Pinning a CAN arm here would fail the gate as a dead pin, which is the intended reading.
_measured_spread: Re-measured for the seam-counting instrument (#2134) over 5 process invocations (3, 5, 5, 5 and 3 repetitions) on one host (g++ 13.3.0, Release). CROSS-RUN: every pinned row's median was byte-identical across all five, 0 B. IN-RUN: every pinned row read min = max, except udp-rope-pool link_base, where one repetition in each of two invocations read 1896 B against a 232 B median (a one-off draw; the gate reads medians). The high-water columns stay unpinned: tcp-server hw_peak moved 24874..65864 across runs and ws-server hw_peak 107000..139656, so a band on either would fire on a transient buffer, not on a connection's cost.
_repin_2134: Re-pinned 2026-10-14 (#2134) when the instrument began counting through the link's injected sources. On the default slab root the operator-new counter alone saw only whole 256 KiB slabs, so a median could read 0 or one slab. Counted now through each link's memory seam and charged at the slab class: tcp-server per_conn 280 B (unchanged), ws-server 392 B (+16 B, class rounding against the old usable-size count), and link_base 2648 B on both, against 464 B at the previous pin. A heap-rooted build (kSlabPool false, kArenaBytes 0) reads 2608 B there, so that growth landed while the instrument was blind; it is recorded here, not introduced by the re-pin. Medians were byte-identical across 5 invocations (3, 5, 5, 5 and 3 repetitions), g++ 13.3.0, Release. The link_base growth is tracked as #2156 (per-link base RAM grew unseen; find and shrink).
_band_rationale: 8 B, kept from the previous instrument (2x its widest 4 B spread). The seam counter charges each block at its kSizeClasses row, 16 B apart below 256 B, so a per-connection block that moves up one class reads at least +16 B and trips the band; growth inside a class reads 0 and costs no RAM on the slab root. The 0.5% term exists only for the two ~64 KB udp link_base rows (~328 B there): a caller-sized buffer whose allocator overhead a libc packaging change can move without any design regression.
_toolchain: These figures contain the sizeof of every transport, so they are compiler- and allocator-bound. Measured on a different toolchain than the pin, the gate reports drift but enforces in warn mode only — an unattributable difference must never red main.

activation.criterion: Flip perf-local.yml's `--mode warn` to `--mode fail` once 20 consecutive pinned-host samples have been banked with no unexplained RAM_CENSUS_GATE warning AND the pins have been re-taken on the bench host's own toolchain. 20 points is about a release's worth of main pushes here, which is the same evidence bar the Cortex-M0 drift check set before its own flip. Until then a threshold picked before the noise is known is the unreachable-budget failure mode this repo already hit once.
activation.whole_node_census: bench_ram_census_tcp is TREND-ONLY and deliberately has no pins. It gains a ratchet only after this one has proven quiet — do not read its published series as gated.

_repin_2156: Re-pinned 2026-10-15 (#2156) after the stream servers stopped drawing an unused 8-slot send ring and their poll set stopped being sized to the whole admission cap up front. link_base 2648 B -> 664 B on tcp-server and ws-server (the object plus the poll set's first block). The poll set now grows to exactly fit the slot table as peers are admitted, so that cost moved from link_base into per_conn at its true size: tcp-server per_conn and after_td 280 -> 290 B, ws-server 392 -> 402 B at K=8. Every other row is unchanged. Medians byte-identical across 3 invocations of 5 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2163: Re-pinned 2026-10-15 (#2163) after the UDP default max_frame became one MTU (1,472 B) instead of 64 KiB, which sizes the receive segment and scratch: udp-span link_base 65768 B -> 1768 B and udp-rope-heap 65816 B -> 1768 B. Medians byte-identical across 3 invocations of 5 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2144: Re-pinned 2026-10-16 (#2144) when the stream links moved onto the shared-frame egress, one ring per (peer, vertex). A ring is drawn only while that vertex has frames waiting, so an idle session holds just its 24 B egress slot in place of the old 1 B stall streak: tcp-server per_conn and after_td 290 -> 306 B at K=8 (the session grows 64 -> 80 B); ws-server stays at 402 B, its session having dropped its own write state. The link no longer carries a write mutex or a handoff queue: link_base 664 -> 584 B on both. Medians byte-identical across 3 invocations of 5 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2144_on_2176: Re-pinned 2026-10-17 (#2144) when the shared-frame egress was replayed onto #2176's WS frame ingress. That change removed the WS session's stream buffer and with it the padding that had absorbed the 24 B egress slot, so the slot now shows on the WS row as it already did on TCP: ws-server per_conn and after_td 402 -> 434 B at K=8 (the session is 368 B, one block class up). Every other row is unchanged. Medians byte-identical across 3 invocations of 9 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2141: Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#2141) when the TCP server and the self-healing links moved onto the frame-ingress module. The session's receive state is now one frame_ingress_t (header slot and body cursor) and the body is drawn at its exact size and handed off on delivery, so nothing is retained between frames: tcp-server per_conn and after_td 306 -> 290 B at K=8. Every other row is unchanged. Medians byte-identical across 5 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2198: Re-pinned 2026-10-17 (#2198) when the stream links gained the application's liveness check. Each link carries its frozen-close count and its one-peer liveness record (8 B each; the one-peer progress flag sits in an existing hole): link_base 584 -> 600 B on tcp-server and ws-server. Per peer, the session's liveness record adds 8 B and its three progress flags sit in padding; per_conn and after_td are unchanged at K=8 (290 B tcp-server, 434 B ws-server, inside their block classes). Medians byte-identical across 3 invocations of 9 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
_repin_2142: Re-pinned 2026-10-18 (#2142) when the UDP link stopped drawing a receive scratch and a state scratch at start. A borrowed-span link (no rope sink) in a build that opts in to config_t::kUdpStackScratchBytes (the bench preset binds 16 KiB; the library default is 0) receives each datagram into stack scratch and delivers it borrowed: udp-span link_base 1768 -> 216 B, the link object alone (sizeof 224 -> 216 B with the state source gone). A rope link keeps one held segment sized to max_frame (1,472 B by default, a 1,536 B block): udp-rope-heap 1768 -> 1752 B, udp-rope-pool 232 -> 216 B (its segment comes from the pool, counted at the pool). Syscalls and copies per datagram are unchanged. Medians byte-identical across 5 repetitions, g++ 13.3.0, Release, default slab root.
